To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) pregnant women who use alcohol and/or other drugs are at risk for adverse health and social outcomes for both themselves and their children, and 2) evidence-based psychosocial and pharmacological interventions are effective for reducing substance use and associated problems in pregnant women.

substance abuse treatment for pregnant women is effective and that the most effective treatments include behavioral and psychosocial components, and address co-occurring disorders and trauma exposure.
universal screening, comprehensive assessment, and evidence-based treatment are essential for improving health outcomes for women who abuse alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs during pregnancy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of women who use substances during pregnancy and their treatment needs.
the development, evaluation, implementation, and dissemination of evidence-based interventions for substance abuse treatment services for women who are pregnant or parenting young children.
the development, implementation and evaluation of effective psychosocial and pharmacotherapeutic interventions for substance abusing pregnant women and women of reproductive age.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are effective substance abuse treatments for pregnant women.
there is strong evidence for the effectiveness of psychosocia l and behavioral substance abuse treatment services for substance-using pregnant women.
there is sufficient evidence to support the efficacy of behavioral interventions for pregnant women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is strong evidence for the effectiveness of behavioral and psychosocial substance abuse treatments in reducing substance use during pregnancy, and that these services are most effective when integrated with other medical and psychosocial services.
there is a need to increase the number of treatment programs that offer specialized services for substance abusing pregnant women.

the most effective treatment for pregnant women with substance use disorder is a multidisciplinary approach, including medical, psychiatric, and substance abuse treatment, and that this treatment must be tailored to the individual patient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one size fits all approach to treating pregnant women with substance use disorders.
we can and do make a difference in the lives of pregnant women who are using substances.
there are many evidence-based approaches to treating pregnant substance users and their children that are available to the field.
